goal.objective:
`src/csv.js` must export `parse`, `stringify`, `escapeField` and the error class `CsvError`. `parse(text, options)` returns an array of records, each an array of field strings. A leading U+FEFF byte-order mark is dropped; anywhere else U+FEFF is ordinary data. Records are terminated by CRLF, LF or a lone CR, and a single terminator at the very end of the document closes the last record without starting an empty one, so `"a\n"` and `"a"` both read as one record while `"a\n\n"` reads as two and `"\n"` reads as one record holding one empty field. An empty document has no records at all. Fields are never trimmed, and an empty field is preserved wherever it appears, including at the start or end of a record.

A field is quoted only when the quote character is its very first character: there, the field runs to the matching closing quote, a doubled quote character stands for one literal quote, and delimiters and line terminators inside the quotes are data rather than separators. A quote character anywhere else in a field is ordinary text. After a closing quote only a delimiter, a line terminator or the end of the document may follow. `options.delimiter` (default `,`) and `options.quote` (default `"`) each take one UTF-16 code unit; they must differ from each other and neither may be a line terminator. `options.strictWidth` makes every record after the first have to match the first record's field count; without it ragged records are returned as they are.

Every failure throws `CsvError`. Positional failures carry a 1-based `line` and, where a single character is at fault, a 1-based `column` counted in UTF-16 code units from the start of that line: `unterminated quoted field` points at the opening quote, and `unexpected character after closing quote: b` points at the offending character, both accounting for line breaks that occurred inside a quoted field. `expected 2 fields, got 1` carries the line the offending record starts on. Bad arguments throw without a position: `input must be a string`, `delimiter must be a single character`, `quote must be a single character`, `delimiter and quote must differ`, `delimiter and quote must not be line terminators`.

`escapeField(value, options)` returns the text for one field. A string is used as it is; `null` and `undefined` become the empty field; booleans and finite numbers are converted with `String`; anything else throws (`unsupported field value: NaN` for non-finite numbers, `unsupported field type: object` otherwise). The field is quoted, doubling every embedded quote character, when it contains the delimiter, the quote character, CR, LF or U+FEFF, or when `options.alwaysQuote` is set. `stringify(rows, options)` writes each record's escaped fields joined by the delimiter and followed by `options.newline` (default CRLF, and it must be CRLF, LF or CR), including after the last record, and prepends the byte-order mark when `options.bom` is set. `stringify` throws `CsvError` for input that is not an array (`rows must be an array`), a record that is not an array (`record 1 is not an array`) and a record with no fields (`record 0 has no fields`). Reading a document this module wrote, with the same options, must return exactly the records it was given. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You implement one program task in the workspace you are given, against its own test suite, and you stop when the tests pass.

The workspace is your working directory: every bash command and every file path resolves inside it, so read and edit its files by their relative paths and never search outside it.


Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

1: import test from 'node:test';
2: import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
3: 
4: import { CsvError, escapeField, parse, stringify } from '../src/csv.js';
5: 
6: /** Deterministic 32-bit PRNG so the generated cases are identical on every run. */
7: function mulberry32(seed) {
8:   let a = seed >>> 0;
9:   return () => {
10:     a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) >>> 0;
11:     let t = Math.imul(a ^ (a >>> 15), 1 | a);
12:     t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t;
13:     return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
14:   };
15: }
16: 
17: function caught(fn) {
18:   try {
19:     fn();
20:   } catch (error) {
21:     return error;
22:   }
23:   throw new Error('expected the call to throw');
24: }
25: 
26: test('reads plain records', () => {
27:   assert.deepStrictEqual(parse('a,b,c\n1,2,3\n'), [
28:     ['a', 'b', 'c'],
29:     ['1', '2', '3'],
30:   ]);
31: });
32: 
33: test('record termination', () => {
34:   const cases = [
35:     ['a\n', [['a']]],
36:     ['a', [['a']]],
37:     ['a\n\n', [['a'], ['']]],
38:     ['\n', [['']]],
39:     ['a,b\r\nc,d', [['a', 'b'], ['c', 'd']]],
40:     ['a\rb', [['a'], ['b']]],
41:     ['a\r\n', [['a']]],
42:     ['a\n\rb\n', [['a'], [''], ['b']]],
43:   ];
44:   for (const [text, expected] of cases) assert.deepStrictEqual(parse(text), expected, JSON.stringify(text));
45: });
46: 
47: test('the shape of a document', () => {
48:   const cases = [
49:     ['', []],
50:     ['\ufeff', []],
51:     ['\ufeffa,b\n', [['a', 'b']]],
52:     ['a,\ufeffb\n', [['a', '\ufeffb']]],
53:     ['a,,b', [['a', '', 'b']]],
54:     [',', [['', '']]],
55:     ['a,', [['a', '']]],
56:     [',a', [['', 'a']]],
57:   ];
58:   for (const [text, expected] of cases) assert.deepStrictEqual(parse(text), expected, JSON.stringify(text));
59: });
60: 
61: test('quoted fields carry delimiters, terminators and doubled quotes', () => {
62:   const cases = [
63:     ['"a,b",c\n', [['a,b', 'c']]],
64:     ['"line\nbreak",x\n', [['line\nbreak', 'x']]],
65:     ['"a""b"\n', [['a"b']]],
66:     ['"",""\n', [['', '']]],
67:     ['"a\r\nb"', [['a\r\nb']]],
68:     [' "a",b', [[' "a"', 'b']]],
69:     ['a"b,c', [['a"b', 'c']]],
70:   ];
71:   for (const [text, expected] of cases) assert.deepStrictEqual(parse(text), expected, JSON.stringify(text));
72: });
73: 
74: test('fields are never trimmed', () => {
75:   assert.deepStrictEqual(parse(' a , b \n'), [[' a ', ' b ']]);
76: });
77: 
78: test('astral characters and combining marks survive without normalisation', () => {
79:   assert.deepStrictEqual(parse('\u{1f600},"caf\u00e9",cafe\u0301\n'), [['\u{1f600}', 'caf\u00e9', 'cafe\u0301']]);
80: });
81: 
82: test('an unterminated quoted field reports the opening quote', () => {
83:   const error = caught(() => parse('a,b\nc,"d,e'));
84:   assert.ok(error instanceof CsvError);
85:   assert.match(error.message, /unterminated quoted field/);
86:   assert.equal(error.line, 2);
87:   assert.equal(error.column, 3);
88: });
89: 
90: test('text after a closing quote reports its own position', () => {
91:   const first = caught(() => parse('"a"b'));
92:   assert.match(first.message, /unexpected character after closing quote: b/);
93:   assert.equal(first.line, 1);
94:   assert.equal(first.column, 4);
95:   const later = caught(() => parse('x\n"a\nb"c'));
96:   assert.equal(later.line, 3);
97:   assert.equal(later.column, 3);
98: });
99: 
100: test('the dialect is configurable', () => {
101:   assert.deepStrictEqual(parse('a;b\n', { delimiter: ';' }), [['a', 'b']]);
102:   assert.deepStrictEqual(parse('a\tb\n', { delimiter: '\t' }), [['a', 'b']]);
103:   assert.deepStrictEqual(parse("'a;b';c", { delimiter: ';', quote: "'" }), [['a;b', 'c']]);
104:   assert.deepStrictEqual(parse('"a";b', { delimiter: ';', quote: "'" }), [['"a"', 'b']]);
105: });
106: 
107: test('an invalid dialect is rejected', () => {
108:   assert.throws(() => parse('a', { delimiter: ',,' }), /delimiter must be a single character/);
109:   assert.throws(() => parse('a', { delimiter: '' }), /delimiter must be a single character/);
110:   assert.throws(() => parse('a', { quote: 'ab' }), /quote must be a single character/);
111:   assert.throws(() => parse('a', { delimiter: ',', quote: ',' }), /delimiter and quote must differ/);
112:   assert.throws(() => parse('a', { delimiter: '\n' }), /must not be line terminators/);
113:   assert.throws(() => parse(42), /input must be a string/);
114: });
115: 
116: test('ragged records are allowed unless strictWidth is set', () => {
117:   assert.deepStrictEqual(parse('a,b\nc\n'), [['a', 'b'], ['c']]);
118:   const error = caught(() => parse('a,b\nc\nd,e\n', { strictWidth: true }));
119:   assert.match(error.message, /expected 2 fields, got 1/);
120:   assert.equal(error.line, 2);
121:   assert.deepStrictEqual(parse('a,b\nc,d\n', { strictWidth: true }), [
122:     ['a', 'b'],
123:     ['c', 'd'],
124:   ]);
125: });
126: 
127: test('escapeField quotes exactly the fields that need it', () => {
128:   const cases = [
129:     ['plain', 'plain'],
130:     ['', ''],
131:     [' pad ', ' pad '],
132:     ['a,b', '"a,b"'],
133:     ['a"b', '"a""b"'],
134:     ['"', '""""'],
135:     ['a\nb', '"a\nb"'],
136:     ['a\rb', '"a\rb"'],
137:     ['﻿x', '"﻿x"'],
138:     ['a;b', 'a;b'],
139:   ];
140:   for (const [value, expected] of cases) assert.equal(escapeField(value), expected, JSON.stringify(value));
141:   assert.equal(escapeField('a;b', { delimiter: ';' }), '"a;b"');
142:   assert.equal(escapeField('plain', { alwaysQuote: true }), '"plain"');
143:   assert.equal(escapeField("it's", { quote: "'" }), "'it''s'");
144: });
145: 
146: test('escapeField converts the accepted non-string values', () => {
147:   assert.equal(escapeField(null), '');
148:   assert.equal(escapeField(undefined), '');
149:   assert.equal(escapeField(0), '0');
150:   assert.equal(escapeField(-1.5), '-1.5');
151:   assert.equal(escapeField(false), 'false');

172:   assert.throws(() => stringify([['a']], { newline: '\n\n' }), /newline must be a line terminator/);
173: });

176:   const rows = [['﻿a'], ['b']];
177:   assert.deepStrictEqual(parse(stringify(rows)), rows);
178: });

goal.objective:
`src/csv.js` must export `parse`, `stringify`, `escapeField` and the error class `CsvError`. `parse(text, options)` returns an array of records, each an array of field strings. A leading U+FEFF byte-order mark is dropped; anywhere else U+FEFF is ordinary data. Records are terminated by CRLF, LF or a lone CR, and a single terminator at the very end of the document closes the last record without starting an empty one, so `"a\n"` and `"a"` both read as one record while `"a\n\n"` reads as two and `"\n"` reads as one record holding one empty field. An empty document has no records at all. Fields are never trimmed, and an empty field is preserved wherever it appears, including at the start or end of a record.

A field is quoted only when the quote character is its very first character: there, the field runs to the matching closing quote, a doubled quote character stands for one literal quote, and delimiters and line terminators inside the quotes are data rather than separators. A quote character anywhere else in a field is ordinary text. After a closing quote only a delimiter, a line terminator or the end of the document may follow. `options.delimiter` (default `,`) and `options.quote` (default `"`) each take one UTF-16 code unit; they must differ from each other and neither may be a line terminator. `options.strictWidth` makes every record after the first have to match the first record's field count; without it ragged records are returned as they are.

Every failure throws `CsvError`. Positional failures carry a 1-based `line` and, where a single character is at fault, a 1-based `column` counted in UTF-16 code units from the start of that line: `unterminated quoted field` points at the opening quote, and `unexpected character after closing quote: b` points at the offending character, both accounting for line breaks that occurred inside a quoted field. `expected 2 fields, got 1` carries the line the offending record starts on. Bad arguments throw without a position: `input must be a string`, `delimiter must be a single character`, `quote must be a single character`, `delimiter and quote must differ`, `delimiter and quote must not be line terminators`.

`escapeField(value, options)` returns the text for one field. A string is used as it is; `null` and `undefined` become the empty field; booleans and finite numbers are converted with `String`; anything else throws (`unsupported field value: NaN` for non-finite numbers, `unsupported field type: object` otherwise). The field is quoted, doubling every embedded quote character, when it contains the delimiter, the quote character, CR, LF or U+FEFF, or when `options.alwaysQuote` is set. `stringify(rows, options)` writes each record's escaped fields joined by the delimiter and followed by `options.newline` (default CRLF, and it must be CRLF, LF or CR), including after the last record, and prepends the byte-order mark when `options.bom` is set. `stringify` throws `CsvError` for input that is not an array (`rows must be an array`), a record that is not an array (`record 1 is not an array`) and a record with no fields (`record 0 has no fields`). Reading a document this module wrote, with the same options, must return exactly the records it was given. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.
